source_snapshot.procedure: Download/install openbmc-tools and run `openbmctool ... certificate replace authority ldap -f <File>` using literal default-looking root credentials.
source_snapshot.criteria: The command and certificate upload succeed. A generic note refers to replacing certificate plus private key, while the file-specific line says the PEM contains only certificate.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes a sensitive replace but contradicts the file-specific certificate-only line by requiring/claiming a cert-private-key pair, exposes BMC credentials and relies on HTTP status without active state, implementation branch, LDAPS/auth or rollback proof.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with CRITICAL risk correctly requires resolution of authority role/file format, protected material validation, one replace, active metadata, bounded service impact, live TLS/auth/local fallback and rollback, but assumed atomicity before the pinned source implementation was checked.

old_problem: The Master contains a generic certificate-plus-key sentence but a specific certificate-only file line; DeepSeek chooses the unsafe cert-plus-key interpretation. Prior review also could not prove that `replace` exists or differs from `update`, and described atomic replacement without source confirmation. Command success cannot prove the intended LDAP authority object, active fingerprint, live trust or recovery.
disposition_reason: Pinned openbmctool source code resolves every core ambiguity. `certificate replace authority ldap` is a real subcommand whose example uses `Root-CA.pem`. On Redfish-capable targets it calls CertificateService.ReplaceCertificate for `/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/Truststore/Certificates/1`; on legacy targets it performs DELETE then PUT and is explicitly not atomic. `update` uses a different collection POST/legacy PUT path. The Review layer therefore requires certificate-only CA material, pre-verification of the exact branch and target object, mode-specific safety/recovery, active trust and live authentication. Project target values remain readiness inputs.
decision_basis: XLSX row 934, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, adjacent Update/View-User rows and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed; row 935 and its manifest identity were independently verified.

Pinned openbmctool source defines the replace subcommand and Root-CA example, selects the LDAP authority trust-store object, and shows a Redfish ReplaceCertificate branch versus a legacy DELETE-then-PUT branch. This is authoritative command behavior, not an inferred synonym for Update.
The source code proves the legacy branch is not atomic and the Redfish branch hardcodes certificate object `/1`; both facts require target preflight and stronger recovery than HTTP-status acceptance.
RFC 4513 requires live LDAP TLS server-certificate and identity validation. Active fingerprint plus allowed/denied/role/local-fallback tests are required after the write.

test_case.test_name: Replace one verified OpenBMC LDAP root CA object with certificate-only PEM using mode-specific recovery
test_case.purpose: Verify that one approved pinned `certificate replace authority ldap` replaces the exact intended LDAP authority trust object with an approved certificate-only root CA, follows the verified Redfish or legacy implementation branch without false atomicity claims, activates the correct fingerprint, preserves unrelated trust, restores secure LDAP authentication/roles and retains independent local recovery.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware identity and pinned reviewed openbmctool commit with recorded `redfishSupportPresent` branch behavior
For Redfish mode, proof that Truststore Certificates/1 is the exact intended LDAP authority object; for legacy mode, documented DELETE/PUT endpoint semantics and outage/recovery acceptance
Approved certificate-only LDAP root-CA PEM with no private key, exact fingerprint, subject/issuer, validity, algorithm and target-supported chain/file format
LDAPS FQDN/port, server certificate identity/SAN, served chain, issuer and TLS policy matching the proposed CA
Complete redacted active/pending LDAP trust inventory, LDAP config/mappings/auth policy/sessions and unrelated-certificate baseline
Protected BMC/file handling on an isolated trusted management path because the pinned function disables HTTPS verification, plus independent target identity evidence
Independent local-admin/console recovery, preserved prior CA material and separately approved exact rollback
Allowed/denied LDAP user, role mapping, local fallback and bounded reconnect/outage matrix
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL TRUST-STORE REPLACEMENT; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT POINT-OF-ACTION APPROVAL. Preserve logs and export the complete redacted trust/LDAP/auth baseline. Pin and inspect openbmctool, determine its Redfish versus legacy branch before the action, and verify the exact target object: Redfish `/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/Truststore/Certificates/1` must match the current intended LDAP CA; the legacy endpoint must have an approved DELETE-then-PUT outage/recovery plan. Because the pinned code disables HTTPS verification, use only an approved isolated trusted management path with independently verified BMC identity; never expose source credentials. Validate certificate-only PEM, approved fingerprint and absence of private-key blocks, and validate the LDAPS server chain/identity. After approval, perform one replace, capture redacted response/audit and bounded reconnect/outage timeline, then read back active/pending trust inventory and exact fingerprint. Prove LDAPS hostname/chain enforcement, allowed login/role, invalid denial and local-admin fallback. Restore prior CA only through separate approval. Never claim atomicity for legacy mode, bypass LDAPS verification, clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Exactly the pre-verified LDAP authority object is replaced by the approved certificate-only CA fingerprint, with unrelated trust objects unchanged and no private key processed or exposed. Redfish mode completes through the expected ReplaceCertificate target; legacy mode records its delete/put gap and recovers within the approved bound without an atomicity claim. The new CA is active, the intended LDAPS server chain and identity validate, allowed/denied/role behavior is correct, local administration remains available and the approved final or rollback state is fully proven.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires certificate-only validation, verified implementation branch and target object, one approved replace, mode-specific response/audit/timeline, exact active fingerprint and inventory reconciliation, live LDAPS chain/identity plus allowed/denied/role/local tests, and final/rollback proof. HTTP 200 or `Replace complete` alone cannot pass. Wrong `/1` object/legacy endpoint, private-key presence, partial or unexpected deletion, incorrect/inactive CA, unrelated trust change, TLS/auth/role failure, local lockout, secret exposure or inability to restore is FAIL and stops. Missing branch/object authority, isolation, CA, recovery or approval is NOT READY.
safety_gate: Reject any private-key block; `authority ldap` replacement uses the approved certificate-only root-CA file for this pinned contract.
Verify the tool-selected branch and exact certificate object before the write. Never assume hardcoded Redfish index 1 or the legacy endpoint is the intended slot.
Treat legacy DELETE then PUT as non-atomic and potentially outage-causing; require console recovery and preserved prior CA before approval.
Because the pinned function uses unverified HTTPS, restrict execution to an explicitly approved isolated trusted management path with independent target identity, or do not execute.
Stop on timeout, partial state, wrong object, chain/hostname failure, unexpected auth/role or recovery impact; do not retry, substitute Update or clear evidence.
expected_evidence: Approval, target/firmware, pinned source commit/hash, detected Redfish/legacy branch and exact target-object proof
Certificate-only PEM/no-private-key validation, approved CA fingerprint/metadata and LDAPS server identity/chain comparison
Complete redacted before/after trust inventory, one replace response/audit and Redfish action or legacy delete/put timeline
Active/pending fingerprint/slot readback, unrelated trust unchanged and bounded service/reconnect evidence
Trusted LDAPS hostname/chain, allowed login/role, invalid denial, local fallback, final/rollback state and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong target object, partial legacy delete/put, inactive CA, TLS/auth failure or access loss, stop without retry. Use independent console/local administration to restore the exact preserved prior certificate-only CA through the pre-approved mode-specific procedure, verify active fingerprint and complete inventory, then prove LDAPS and local access. Preserve audit/timeline evidence; never upload a private key, substitute Update silently or disable certificate validation.

source_conflict.reason: The file-specific certificate-only line agrees with pinned source examples (`Root-CA.pem`) and authority trust-store targeting; the generic cert-plus-key sentence and DeepSeek pair claim are inapplicable copied text. Pinned code also proves Replace is distinct from Update and exposes Redfish versus non-atomic legacy semantics.
